question: How does a joint venture differ from standard facility outsourcing?

question: What is an important goal when assessing a patient with neurasthenia?

options.D: Urine elimination and sexual reproduction

question: A nurse needs to weigh a patient wearing a heavy leg cast that cannot be taken off. How should this be documented?

options.C: It automatically increases the clinic budget allocation.
options.D: It results in the immediate suspension of the senior nurse.

explanation: Guessed data leads to bad government decisions. If the numbers say you treated 50 kids for malaria when it was actually 500, the next drug supply shipment will be way too small!

question: Why is a longitudinal design great for studying chronic illnesses like heart disease?

options.A: It costs almost no money compared to other study methods
options.B: It guarantees that every single patient will be completely cured
options.C: It allows researchers to watch how the disease develops and progresses slowly over time
options.D: It requires only one afternoon of data collection at a clinic

explanation: Well done! Since chronic illnesses unfold gradually, tracking patients over a long period helps us understand the disease process clearly.

question: Which of the following is a direct surveillance responsibility for a clinical nurse?

options.A: Enforcing federal health policies in the national parliament
options.B: Importing international vaccines for national distribution
options.C: Conducting post-mortem examinations on all deceased patients
options.D: Reporting suspected cases of priority diseases immediately

explanation: Nurses must promptly notify public health authorities when they encounter suspected cases of dangerous or reportable diseases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T19#GNS313_U1_T19_h6)

question: Why does the law make reporting certain infectious diseases compulsory for health workers?

options.A: To allow early government action to stop epidemics from spreading
options.B: To increase the financial taxes collected from local hospitals
options.C: To punish patients who contract preventable bacterial infections
options.D: To create extra paperwork for overworked nursing staff

explanation: Exactly! Quick reporting gives public health teams the heads-up they need to step in and contain an outbreak before it gets out of hand.

question: What role does the school nurse commonly play in supporting student mental health?

options.A: Grading students on mental health examinations
options.B: Observing behavioral shifts and listening to concerns
options.C: Conducting formal psychiatric hospital admissions
options.D: Prescribing antidepressant medications to students

explanation: Nurses are often the first to notice emotional distress and provide a safe listening space or referral when needed. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main characteristic of a common vehicle outbreak?

options.A: Infection only spreads slowly from one family member to another over months
options.B: Pathogens travel exclusively through the air as dry microscopic dust
options.C: The disease can only be caught by direct physical contact in a hospital
options.D: Many people become infected simultaneously from a single contaminated source

explanation: Because a single food or water source serves many individuals, a common vehicle outbreak typically results in a sudden surge of cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of primary healthcare centers in Nigeria?

options.A: Basic preventive services and community health
options.B: Complex neurosurgeries and organ transplants
options.C: Long-term rehabilitation for chronic stroke
options.D: Advanced medical research and drug trials

explanation: Primary health centers handle grassroots care, immunizations, and treatment of common minor conditions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is a mineral-based drug commonly used to neutralize stomach acid?

options.A: Penicillin G
options.B: Morphine sulfate
options.C: Digoxin extract
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Calcium carbonate is a mineral compound often found in over-the-counter antacids to quickly soothe heartburn.

question: As a Nigerian nurse, what is a key part of your role when it comes to community nutrition?

options.A: Formulating industrial food additives in factories
options.B: Replacing all traditional farming with foreign grains
options.C: Educating communities and managing cases of malnutrition
options.D: Exporting local cash crops to international markets

explanation: That's right! Nurses are frontline educators. We spot nutritional gaps in our clinics and teach mothers the best ways to feed their families.

question: Why are antibiotics often started right away before lab results are even back?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of laboratory diagnostic supplies
options.B: To completely eliminate the need for any follow-up testing
options.C: To cure viral infections like herpes simplex immediately
options.D: To stop the infection from spreading upward into the reproductive tract

explanation: Starting treatment fast prevents the infection from traveling up into the uterus and fallopian tubes, avoiding bigger problems later.

question: A patient is in the secretory phase of her cycle. Which hormone is doing the heavy lifting to keep this phase going?

options.A: FSH
options.B: GnRH
options.C: Testosterone
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: During the secretory phase, progesterone takes center stage to keep the uterine lining rich, thick, and cozy for a fertilized egg.

question: How does the placenta give a newborn temporary protection against common infections?

options.A: By actively transferring maternal IgG antibodies across the placental membrane
options.B: By producing white blood cells that migrate into the fetal bloodstream
options.C: By filtering out all bacteria and viruses from maternal blood
options.D: By stimulating the fetal bone marrow to produce immunoglobulins

explanation: Nature's gift! The placenta lets the mother's protective IgG antibodies pass through to the baby, giving them a helpful head start against infections after birth.

question: What is the first step in the risk management process?

options.A: Patient discharge
options.B: Risk identification
options.C: Staff punishment
options.D: Financial compensation

explanation: You cannot manage a hazard until you first find out it exists by spotting it through reports, audits, or observation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h3)

question: A patient recovering from serum sickness complains of stiff, aching joints. Which nursing action is best?

options.A: Apply ice packs to the joints for twenty minutes every hour
options.B: Massage the inflamed joint firmly to break up the immune complexes
options.C: Keep the affected limbs strictly immobilized in a rigid splint
options.D: Encourage gentle range-of-motion exercises as tolerated

explanation: Gentle movement is wonderful here; it keeps the joints from locking up while giving the tissues space to heal comfortably.

question: How does the stress-relaxation response help an organ like your urinary bladder?

options.A: It forces the organ to empty immediately when it reaches half capacity
options.B: It prevents the muscle cells from ever fatiguing during hard work
options.C: It generates rapid pumping movements to mix internal contents
options.D: It allows the organ to stretch to hold more fluid without a sharp pressure spike

explanation: This clever response lets your bladder gradually accommodate more fluid as it fills up, preventing sudden uncomfortable pressure spikes. Nursing clinicals will make this super clear too!

question: A patient complains of mild tummy cramping and bloating shortly after a colonoscopy. What is the usual cause?

options.A: A severe allergic reaction to the sedative medication used
options.B: Internal bleeding starting in the lower intestinal wall
options.C: An infection caused by unsterilised examination tools
options.D: Air introduced into the bowel during the procedure to improve visibility

explanation: Nothing to panic about! Doctors pump a little air inside to see the bowel walls clearly, which causes temporary bloating until the air passes out.

question: Why do pregnant women routinely need iron supplements during gestation?

options.A: To harden the bones of the mother's hands and feet
options.B: To increase the amount of amniotic fluid in the womb
options.C: To support the significant increase in maternal blood volume
options.D: To prevent the baby from developing gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! A pregnant woman's body makes a lot more blood to support the baby, and iron helps prevent anemia during this heavy workload.

question: Why do nurses watch out specifically for waterborne diseases after heavy floods?

options.A: Excessive rainfall permanently destroys all local mosquito breeding grounds
options.B: Overflowing sewage systems mix with and contaminate drinking water sources
options.C: Damp weather conditions cause rapid airborne transmission of influenza
options.D: Standing water causes an immediate drop in local atmospheric oxygen levels

explanation: Floodwaters easily ruin sanitation systems, letting sewage leak into drinking water and spreading dangerous germs. Great to keep in mind for community health!

question: A nurse notices morning shift surgical patients report less pain than evening ones. Why is this a good research problem?

options.A: It highlights a noticeable pattern and potential gap in pain management routines
options.B: It proves that evening nurses are performing their duties incorrectly
options.C: It guarantees a promotion for the nurse who records the observation
options.D: It eliminates the need to administer prescribed pain medications

explanation: Spotting differences in patient care across shifts points to a real clinical puzzle worth investigating. You're thinking like a true researcher!

question: Why might a newly graduated nurse hesitate to accept delegated duties from a senior colleague?

options.A: Fear of failure and lack of professional self-confidence
options.B: Belief that delegation is illegal in all healthcare facilities
options.C: Desire to take over the senior colleague's official management title
options.D: Preference for administrative paperwork over direct patient care

explanation: It's totally normal for fresh grads to feel nervous! Doubts usually stem from a lack of confidence and the fear of making mistakes early on.

question: What is a key visual difference between a bar chart and a histogram?

options.A: Histograms have touching bars because data is continuous
options.B: Histograms are only used for nominal data categories
options.C: Bar charts display changes over time on the vertical axis
options.D: Bar charts use circles instead of rectangular bars

explanation: Because histograms represent continuous numerical ranges, their bars touch each other to show that the scale flows without gaps. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h6)

question: What makes a disease carrier different from a regular clinical patient?

options.A: Carriers harbor pathogens without showing any symptoms of illness
options.B: Carriers only transmit infections through contaminated water supplies
options.C: Clinical cases always recover faster than healthy carriers
options.D: Clinical cases never shed pathogens into the environment

explanation: Carriers feel and look completely well, which is why they can unknowingly spread germs. It is a sneaky way infections move around!

question: How do qualitative researchers usually find key insights in interview texts?

options.A: By searching for recurring themes and patterns in text transcripts
options.B: By calculating the mean and standard deviation of blood tests
options.C: By running computer programs that solve complex algebra equations
options.D: By measuring the exact dosage of medication given to patients

explanation: Instead of crunching numbers, qualitative researchers read carefully through transcripts to find common themes and powerful quotes.

question: How do most medicines actually produce their effects in our body?

options.A: By altering existing physiological processes
options.B: By changing the genetic code of human cells
options.C: By completely replacing natural body hormones
options.D: By creating entirely new cellular functions

explanation: Drugs don't usually invent brand new jobs for cells. Instead, they speed up or slow down things your body is already doing naturally!

question: Why do state or regional health schemes often exist alongside a national scheme?

options.A: To address local health priorities and specific regional demographics
options.B: To compete directly with private international clinics
options.C: To prevent rural residents from visiting city hospitals
options.D: To collect extra taxes without government approval

explanation: Correct! State schemes let local governments customize health packages to fit the unique cultural and financial needs of their own people.

question: What term is used for pale, bulky, and foul-smelling stools caused by unabsorbed fats?

options.A: Melena
options.B: Steatorrhea
options.C: Hematochezia
options.D: Glycosuria

explanation: Spot on! Steatorrhea is the clinical word for fatty, greasy stools that happen when the gut fails to properly digest or absorb lipids.

question: During a digestive check, which physical sign is best for quickly spotting dehydration?

options.A: Moisture of the oral mucous membranes
options.B: The presence of minor scars on the skin
options.C: The temperature of the lower legs
options.D: The exact color of the client's hair

explanation: Checking inside the mouth! Dry or sticky gums and tongue are quick, reliable signs that a patient is losing too much fluid from vomiting or diarrhea.

question: Which waste product from the baby is cleared out by the placenta into the mother's circulation?

options.A: Mucus
options.B: Urea
options.C: Bile
options.D: Saliva

explanation: The placenta acts as the baby's temporary kidney, filtering out nitrogen wastes like urea so the mother's kidneys can excrete them. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T5#GNS121_U6_T5_h4)

question: In the popular BUBBLE-EE postpartum assessment guide, what does the second 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bonding
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Bladder
options.D: Bowel

explanation: Remember the checklist: Breasts, Uterus, Bowel, Bladder, Lochia, Episiotomy, Extremities, and Emotions. You'll master this assessment in no time!

question: Where should you place your hands when giving abdominal thrusts to a conscious adult who is choking?

options.A: Across the soft throat area
options.B: Just above the navel
options.C: In the center of the chest
options.D: Directly over the lower ribs

explanation: Correct! Placing your fist just above the belly button (and well below the ribs) lets you push the diaphragm up safely without breaking any bones.

question: What is a common community-level effect when mental health struggles go untreated for too long?

options.A: Higher local crop yields due to increased community labor
options.B: Decreased need for public transportation infrastructure
options.C: Increased strain on emergency services and public health systems
options.D: Immediate elimination of all local economic taxation policies

explanation: Correct! When people don't get support early, emergency rooms, local clinics, and public health resources end up carrying a very heavy load.

question: Why does urine output drop so much during cardiogenic shock?

options.A: The urinary bladder shuts down from nerve damage
options.B: The patient drank too little water
options.C: Kidneys start making solid waste instead
options.D: The body saves remaining blood for the brain and heart by pulling it away from the kidneys

explanation: In an emergency, the body plays survival mode! It redirects what little blood is left away from non-essential organs like the kidneys and skin, saving it all for the brain and heart.

question: Why is protein intake typically increased alongside total calories in stressed clinical states?

options.A: To stimulate the production of red blood cells
options.B: To serve as the primary source of quick cellular energy
options.C: To rebuild damaged tissue and prevent muscle wasting
options.D: To slow down gastrointestinal motility

explanation: Proteins supply the essential building blocks needed to repair wounds and maintain lean body mass during hypermetabolic illness. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T009#GNS227_U6_T009_h3)

question: Which Nigerian law provides major legal protection against domestic violence and harmful practices?

options.A: Standard Nursing and Midwifery Council Decree
options.B: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: Public Health Sanitation and Hygiene Code
options.D: National Health Insurance Authority Act

explanation: The VAPP Act is a key law in Nigeria meant to protect people from violence at home and in public. Good to know for your exams and practice!

question: A confused patient arrives at the emergency department with suspected drug ingestion. What quick bedside check must a nurse perform right away?

options.A: Checking blood glucose level
options.B: Measuring abdominal girth
options.C: Testing deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Checking visual acuity

explanation: Always rule out low blood sugar first! Severe hypoglycemia can look identical to a drug overdose, so a quick finger-prick blood glucose check is a nursing essential.

question: What is the typical physical shape of a rectal suppository?

options.A: Cone or bullet shape
options.B: Rigid metallic cylinder
options.C: Large hollow glass sphere
options.D: Long flat rectangular strip

explanation: Suppositories are molded into rounded, tapering shapes designed for smooth and comfortable insertion into the anal canal. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T5#GNS122_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of performing CPR on a patient in cardiac arrest?

options.A: To cool down the body and protect the brain
options.B: To clear thick mucus from blocked airways
options.C: To restore normal heart rhythm immediately
options.D: To keep oxygenated blood flowing to vital organs

explanation: CPR acts as an artificial pump to circulate remaining oxygen in the blood to the brain and heart until advanced help arrives. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is communication considered a two-way process in the IEC framework?

options.A: It focuses only on passing medical news from the hospital to the village
options.B: It requires two different nurses to speak at the same community meeting
options.C: It means printing health materials in both English and a local language
options.D: It involves listening to community feedback and addressing local fears

explanation: Effective communication in IEC goes beyond just giving orders; it requires listening to what the community has to say and clearing up doubts. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: When is an autocratic leadership style most helpful in a clinical setting?

options.A: During a sudden cardiac arrest code requiring immediate, direct action
options.B: During a monthly staff meeting to discuss cafeteria meal options
options.C: When orienting a brand-new nursing student to basic vital signs
options.D: When planning a flexible holiday roster for the nursing unit

explanation: In an emergency like a cardiac arrest, there's no time for a committee meeting! Autocratic leadership gives clear, fast orders to save lives.

question: What skin pigment protects cells from ultraviolet light damage?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Keratin
options.C: Melanin
options.D: Carotene

explanation: Melanin is produced by melanocytes to absorb harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h2)

question: A patient wanting a medical abortion has an IUD in place. What should the nurse make sure happens first?

options.A: Ensure the IUD is removed prior to starting the misoprostol regimen
options.B: Leave the IUD in because misoprostol will push it out
options.C: Give extra antibiotics to stop local infections
options.D: Switch the patient immediately to vacuum aspiration

explanation: We need to take out any IUD before starting treatment to prevent serious infections or heavy bleeding. Simple and important safety step!

question: Why might a clinical protocol that works wonderfully in an adult surgical ward fail if copied directly into a children's ward?

options.A: Adult patients always recover faster than pediatric patients regardless of care
options.B: Surgical nurses have much higher educational degrees than pediatric nurses
options.C: Children's wards never use standard hospital protocols of any kind
options.D: Different units have unique patient needs, workflows, and environmental contexts

explanation: Every ward has its own unique vibe and patient needs! We always need to tweak a practice to fit the receiving unit rather than copy-pasting blindly.

question: You notice a care assistant rushing an elderly resident through a meal. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Educate the assistant on patient-centered feeding techniques and safety
options.B: Report the assistant to the police for physical abuse immediately
options.C: Ignore the incident since assistants are trained separately
options.D: Take over feeding all residents in the facility personally

explanation: Well done! As a nurse, you supervise support staff. Teaching them the right, gentle way to feed residents ensures safe and dignified care.

question: Which sign is a classic clue that a patient has a respiratory diphtheria infection?

options.A: Uncontrollable whooping sounds during inhalation
options.B: A fluid-filled rash covering the entire trunk
options.C: A thick grey membrane obstructing the throat
options.D: Severe painful muscle spasms and body arching

explanation: You nailed it! Diphtheria forms a tough, greyish membrane in the throat that can dangerousy block airflow and release toxins.

question: What is the best imaging test to check for liver hydatid cysts?

options.A: Electrocardiography
options.B: X-ray fluoroscopy
options.C: Ultrasound
options.D: Positron emission tomography

explanation: Ultrasound is safe and brilliant at spotting fluid-filled cysts hiding inside the liver.

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Regulating fluid balance and supporting nerve and muscle function
options.B: Acting as organic enzymes to speed up chemical digestion
options.C: Providing the structural framework for red blood cell hemoglobin
options.D: Serving as the body's primary emergency source of stored calories

explanation: Correct! Electrolytes like sodium and potassium keep our body fluids balanced and help our nerves and muscles work smoothly without cramping.

question: You see a sudden, sharp spike on a monthly infection rate graph that is normally very flat. What should you suspect first?

options.A: The normal daily fluctuation of a healthy patient
options.B: An isolated event, outbreak, or possible data recording error
options.C: A permanent and irreversible change in hospital policy
options.D: The complete eradication of the infectious disease

explanation: Spot on! Sudden peaks jump out because they don't fit the normal pattern—usually pointing to an outbreak or a quick typo in the log.

question: How do rushed staff and chaotic hospital environments affect patients?

options.A: Patients demand longer clinical consultations
options.B: Patients feel intimidated and hesitate to question busy workers
options.C: Patients feel inspired to volunteer and help prepare medications
options.D: Patients report the hospital to international boards immediately

explanation: Correct! When a ward is super busy and chaotic, patients feel it's rude or risky to slow things down with questions.

question: Why do we as nursing students need to look back at the history of nutrition?

options.A: To learn how to farm and produce raw food crops
options.B: To replace modern laboratory tests with ancient beliefs
options.C: To memorize the exact dates every vitamin was discovered
options.D: To understand how current dietary guidelines were developed

explanation: You got it! Knowing our history helps us see how past observations grew into the solid clinical recommendations we use to help patients today.

question: What does a positive fluid balance indicate for a patient over a twenty-four-hour period?

options.A: Output was greater than intake
options.B: The patient lost too much body weight
options.C: Intake and output were perfectly even
options.D: Intake was greater than output

explanation: A positive balance means more fluid entered the body than was eliminated, leaving a surplus behind. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T19#GNS122_U1_T19_h7)

question: Which cells are the star players in our adaptive (targeted) immune response?

options.A: Adipocytes
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Lymphocytes
options.D: Erythrocytes

explanation: B cells and T cells are types of lymphocytes. They are the smart cells that handle the targeted, long-term memory side of immunity.

question: What do we mean by an 'acute abdomen' in clinical practice?

options.A: Chronic indigestion caused by spicy food
options.B: Sudden, severe abdominal pain that often requires urgent surgery
options.C: A normal feeling of fullness after a large meal
options.D: A mild muscle cramp after heavy exercise

explanation: Spot on! An 'acute abdomen' is a red flag for sudden, severe belly pain that usually means trouble inside, like appendicitis or a perforation, needing quick surgical eyes.

question: A ward manager notices two nurses arguing over shift rosters. What is the best way to handle this?

options.A: Address the conflict constructively by listening to both sides
options.B: Transfer both nurses to night duty immediately without discussion
options.C: Ignore the disagreement because coworkers always argue eventually
options.D: Tell the rest of the staff to avoid interacting with both nurses

explanation: Sweeping arguments under the rug never works. A good leader steps in early, hears out both nurses, and helps them find a fair, peaceful solution.

question: Why do elderly parents in some communities heavily rely on having sons to take care of them in old age?

options.A: Absence of reliable state-sponsored pension schemes
options.B: Higher wages earned exclusively by male workers
options.C: Government laws forcing sons to pay a parent tax
options.D: Mandatory retirement funds managed by community elders

explanation: Without a government pension or social security to fall back on, elderly parents often count on sons and their wives for survival.

question: What classic physical change is often seen with long-term steroid therapy (cushingoid features)?

options.A: Yellowing skin
options.B: Excessive hair loss
options.C: Enlarged hands
options.D: Moon face

explanation: A round, puffy face—often called a 'moon face'—is a classic sign that the body has been exposed to extra corticosteroids over time.

question: What does the lab usually do if the name on a specimen tube doesn't match the request form?

options.A: Fix the typo themselves without informing the ward
options.B: Reject the specimen and request a new collection
options.C: Call the doctor to guess which patient it belongs to
options.D: Process the sample anyway using the bed number

explanation: Labs have zero tolerance for mismatched names because it's a huge safety hazard. They will throw it out and ask for a fresh sample.

question: What is the main goal of doing an economic appraisal in healthcare?

options.A: To compare costs and outcomes of healthcare choices
options.B: To calculate the exact monthly salary of hospital staff
options.C: To reduce the number of patients admitted to the ward
options.D: To diagnose complex medical conditions in a laboratory

explanation: Think of this as checking if a treatment gives you good value. Economic appraisals look at both the money spent and the health benefits gained so hospitals can make smart choices.

question: What is a major risk when a country relies too heavily on international aid for its health care?

options.A: Aid can be unpredictable and subject to changes in donor priorities
options.B: It automatically guarantees universal health coverage for all citizens
options.C: It forces the government to increase local tax rates every month
options.D: It eliminates out-of-pocket spending across all private hospitals

explanation: External funding can shift based on foreign politics, meaning sudden withdrawals can collapse local programs. Building self-reliance is always better!

question: When checking if an unresponsive patient is breathing normally, what is the maximum time a nurse should spend on this?

options.A: One minute
options.B: Thirty seconds
options.C: Ten seconds
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Nice and quick! We check for breathing and a pulse at the same time, but we never want to waste precious seconds—keep it under 10 seconds so compressions aren't delayed.

question: Which group of workers faces the highest daily risk of exposure to bloodborne infections like HIV and Hepatitis B?

options.A: Healthcare workers
options.B: Textile factory weavers
options.C: Road construction workers
options.D: Office administrative staff

explanation: Because we frequently handle needles, sharps, and patient body fluids, healthcare personnel face a higher risk of bloodborne infections. Safety first!

question: What chemical bond in the cystine molecule do cystine-binding thiol drugs break apart?

options.A: Ionic bond
options.B: Peptide bond
options.C: Disulfide bond
options.D: Hydrogen bond

explanation: Thiol medications act like molecular scissors, specifically targeting and cutting the disulfide bond that holds the cystine molecule together. Clever, right?

question: A nurse notices a patient's blood pressure dropping rapidly and calls the doctor using SBAR. What information should be stated in the Recommendation part?

options.A: What action or intervention is needed right now
options.B: A summary of yesterday's nursing shift notes
options.C: The patient's full medical history from childhood
options.D: The exact cost of the patient's hospital room

explanation: Correct! The 'Recommendation' is where you clearly state what you need done right now to help stabilize your patient.

question: A patient remembers their childhood clearly but cannot recall what they ate an hour ago. What kind of memory loss is this?

options.A: Global retrograde amnesia wiping out all past decades
options.B: Anterograde amnesia with preserved remote memory
options.C: Pure procedural amnesia affecting motor skills only
options.D: Transient global amnesia that will resolve in hours

explanation: You've got it! 'Anterograde' means trouble making *new* memories, while older childhood memories ('remote memory') stay safe in the back of the mind.

question: When listening to music, what property of a sound wave tells you whether the note is high or low (pitch)?

options.A: Resonance
options.B: Frequency
options.C: Amplitude
options.D: Velocity

explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz and determines the pitch of a sound. Think of high-frequency sounds as high-pitched, like a baby crying, and low-frequency as deep, like a drum!

question: What do we call an unexpected injury caused by medical care rather than the patient's actual sickness?

options.A: Latent condition
options.B: Near miss
options.C: Sentinel indicator
options.D: Adverse event

explanation: Don't worry, clinical terms can be tricky at first! An adverse event simply means harm that happened because of medical treatment, not the disease itself. You've got this!

question: A nurse smoothly moves from managing an IV drip in the ER to dressing a wound in the surgical ward. What is this nurse showing?

options.A: Avoidance of heavy patient workloads
options.B: Strict adherence to departmental silos
options.C: Inability to focus on one single duty
options.D: Multi-skilling and clinical versatility

explanation: Spot on! Being able to switch tasks across different units proves you have great clinical versatility and multi-skilling abilities.

question: What is a key characteristic of bone pain caused by osteomyelitis?

options.A: It completely disappears when the patient rests in bed
options.B: It shifts to a different bone every few hours
options.C: It is a constant, throbbing pain that worsens with movement
options.D: It only occurs when the patient eats cold foods

explanation: Bone pain from infection is typically deep, constant, throbbing, and intensified by physical activity or pressure on the site. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the main job of the neurotransmitter GABA when you fall asleep?

options.A: Increasing body temperature and heart rate
options.B: Inhibiting wakefulness centers to allow rest
options.C: Triggering the release of cortisol
options.D: Stimulating the reticular activating system

explanation: GABA is your brain's main calming chemical. It dials down the wake-up centers so you can finally relax and sleep.

question: How has the traditional Almajiri system in some parts of Nigeria unfortunately contributed to street children numbers?

options.A: Extreme poverty has stripped away structural support, leaving pupils to beg for survival
options.B: Religious teachers train children specifically to migrate to foreign countries
options.C: The government mandates that all Quranic students live exclusively outdoors
options.D: Boarding facilities for students are overfunded and turn children away

explanation: You're doing great. When the system lacks enough food and shelter resources, young students are left with no choice but to beg on the streets to eat.

question: Which type of surgical sponge is the largest and best for major tummy (abdominal) surgeries?

options.A: Lap sponge
options.B: Neuro patty
options.C: Gauze swab
options.D: Tonsil sponge

explanation: Lap sponges (laparotomy sponges) are large and heavy-duty, designed to handle deep abdominal operations easily.

question: What is the root cause behind most cases of coronary artery disease?

options.A: Infection of the heart valves by bacteria
options.B: Weakening of the heart muscle walls
options.C: Atherosclerosis from fatty plaque buildup
options.D: Enlargement of the right atrium

explanation: Spot on! Cholesterol and fats slowly accumulate inside the arteries over time, narrowing the pathway and making it hard for blood to pass through.

question: What do most cases of colorectal cancer start from?

options.A: Chronic twisting of the sigmoid colon
options.B: Enlarged external hemorrhoids near the anus
options.C: Severe bacterial infections in the appendix
options.D: Benign polyps on the inner lining of the colon

explanation: Spot on! Most colorectal cancers start out as harmless growths called adenomatous polyps that slowly change over many years.

question: If a patient has severe kidney failure, what adjustment would a nurse expect for a drug that is normally cleared by the kidneys?

options.B: Laboratory diagnostic fees

options.D: Direct surgical costs

explanation: Back in the day, hospitals didn't bill separately for nursing care. Instead, they just lumped the cost right into general room and board charges!

question: As a registered nurse working under the team nursing model, what is your primary role on the ward?

options.A: Supervising the doctors during ward rounds
options.B: Performing every single procedure personally for all patients
options.C: Handling only the administrative paperwork for the ward
options.D: Acting as the team leader and taking overall accountability

explanation: Spot on! The registered nurse coordinates the group and takes ultimate responsibility for the care given, even when delegating specific tasks to others. You've got this!

question: Why should a quality improvement team always include someone working right on the hospital floor?

options.A: To secure funding grants for new medical equipment purchases
options.B: To handle all communication with hospital executive management
options.C: To replace the team leader when meetings run too late
options.D: To provide real-world feedback on how changes affect daily workflow

explanation: Spot on! Frontline staff make sure that new ideas are actually realistic and practical for the nurses and aides doing the work every day.

question: Which channel is most appropriate when trying to reach healthcare policymakers?

options.A: Public street flyers and local music concerts
options.B: Concise policy briefs and executive reports
options.C: Detailed laboratory notebooks with raw data
options.D: Personal diary entries kept in a desk drawer

explanation: Policymakers need brief, structured reports that outline problems and practical recommendations quickly. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h8)

question: What is a major clinical indication for the immediate emergency referral of a pregnant woman?

options.A: Severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia
options.B: Mild morning sickness during the first trimester
options.C: Physiological ankle swelling after long standing
options.D: Normal vertex presentation at 36 weeks

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia poses an immediate, life-threatening risk of seizures and stroke, requiring urgent transfer to a facility capable of managing complications. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of food purchasing in nutritional care?

options.A: Minimizing the time spent on meal preparation
options.B: Reducing the variety of meals served daily
options.C: Buying the most expensive ingredients available
options.D: Ensuring access to safe and nutrient-dense foods

explanation: Food purchasing aims to acquire safe, wholesome ingredients that supply the necessary nutrients for good health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T006#GNS227_U3_T006_h1)

question: Which skin sign strongly points to a liver problem or high bilirubin levels?

options.A: Pallor
options.B: Petechiae
options.C: Cyanosis
options.D: Jaundice

explanation: Jaundice gives the skin and eyes a yellowish tint because bilirubin is building up in the body.

question: An unconscious patient arrives at the emergency unit after a head injury and cannot manage their own saliva. What is the main reason to put them on a ventilator?

options.A: Lowering body temperature
options.B: Airway protection
options.C: Treating high blood pressure
options.D: Correcting severe anemia

explanation: When someone is unconscious, they lose reflexes like swallowing and coughing. Putting them on a ventilator protects their airway so they don't aspirate secretions into their lungs. Excellent clinical thinking!

question: What is the primary purpose of using a surgical safety checklist in the labor ward?

options.A: To slow down emergency cesarean sections unnecessarily
options.B: To give doctors extra paperwork to fill out after work
options.C: To make sure vital safety steps are never skipped during care
options.D: To replace the need for professional nursing judgment

explanation: Checklists act as a memory aid to ensure critical safety checks are completed before, during, and after procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T3#GNS312_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why do we use Boolean words like AND and OR when searching research databases?

options.A: To automatically translate foreign language articles into English
options.B: To convert secondary research summaries into primary data tables
options.C: To check if the author of a research paper has a valid license
options.D: To narrow or broaden search results to find relevant articles

explanation: Great work! Words like AND and OR help you filter your search so you don't get drowned in millions of unrelated papers.

question: Why do you need to be extra careful with cleaning liquids on a smart bed?

options.A: Infection control policies do not apply to automated furniture
options.B: Standard hospital beds never require chemical disinfectants
options.C: Smart bed mattresses are made of disposable paper materials
options.D: Smart beds have electronic panels and crevices where liquid can damage components

explanation: Because of all the wires and electronic touchpads, you must clean carefully so liquid doesn't seep inside and break the bed.

question: Why do doctors evaluate fertility after just six months for women aged thirty-five and older?

options.A: The uterine lining becomes too thick for implantation over time
options.B: Ovarian reserve and egg quality naturally decrease faster at this age
options.C: Hormonal contraceptives take longer to leave the body after age thirty-five
options.D: Older women have a higher rate of chronic pelvic infections

explanation: A quicker evaluation is helpful because a woman's egg quality and supply naturally start to decline faster in her late thirties. Keep up the good work!

question: How do inherited degenerative diseases usually progress compared to a sudden injury?

options.A: They alternate randomly between extreme health and sudden failure
options.B: They remain completely stable after the initial onset
options.C: They start quietly and worsen slowly over a long period
options.D: They appear overnight and resolve completely on their own

explanation: Think of it as a slow burn. Unlike sudden accidents, degenerative conditions develop gradually over months or years.

question: In public health, what does disease 'eradication' mean?

options.A: Replacing all synthetic drugs with natural remedies
options.B: Treating all infected patients with herbal medicines
options.C: Worldwide reduction of the infection incidence to zero
options.D: Reduction of cases to zero in a single country only

explanation: Eradication means completely and permanently wiping out the germ and its reservoir everywhere on planet Earth. Gone for good!

question: Which expense usually takes up the biggest slice of a hospital's budget?

options.A: Patient dietary services
options.B: Office stationery supplies
options.C: Facility security contracts
options.D: Healthcare personnel salaries

explanation: Correct! Paying the dedicated nurses, doctors, and support staff who keep the hospital running takes up the largest share of operating costs.

question: What is the main purpose of asset mapping in a community assessment?

options.A: To count how many people have severe mental illnesses
options.B: To find out how much money the local government has stolen
options.C: To locate abandoned buildings for quarantine centers
options.D: To identify existing local strengths and support systems

explanation: Asset mapping focuses on discovering what positive resources, skills, and groups already exist within the community to help solve problems. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why is expanding health insurance a good strategy for improving health sector funding?

options.A: It guarantees free salaries for all international consultants
options.B: It allows hospitals to stop treating poor patients
options.C: It pools risks and reduces direct out-of-pocket spending
options.D: It removes the need for any government tax collection

explanation: Health insurance spreads financial risk across many people, ensuring steady funds for hospitals while protecting individuals from sudden huge bills. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h7)

question: What is the best way to care for a newborn's umbilical cord stump at home?

options.A: Applying red palm oil daily to speed up cord separation
options.B: Keeping the stump clean and dry without harmful substances
options.C: Dressing the base tightly with herbal mixtures and ash
options.D: Washing the cord aggressively with strong medicated soap

explanation: Just keep it clean and dry! Putting traditional substances like palm oil, herbs, or ash on the cord can introduce dangerous bacteria and lead to newborn tetanus.

question: Why shouldn't you fill a sharps container past its fill line?

options.A: It prevents the hospital from recycling the plastic material
options.B: It makes the container too heavy for the waste collectors
options.C: It increases the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It causes the plastic walls of the container to melt

explanation: You got it! Overfilling sharps bins means needles start poking out or pushing against the lid, putting anyone handling the bin at high risk of a needle-stick injury.

question: Which fatal bacterial infection is a major risk when FGM is done with dirty tools in unsterile environments?

options.A: Tetanus
options.B: Typhoid fever
options.C: Cholera
options.D: Malaria

explanation: Great job! Tetanus spores love dirt and unsterilized gear, making tetanus a huge and dangerous risk during traditional surgeries.

question: Why do nurses collect data during quality improvement projects on the ward?

options.A: To prove a brand-new medical theory through controlled trials
options.B: To fulfill mandatory paperwork requirements for the government
options.C: To track the results of small, continuous changes in clinical workflows
options.D: To punish staff members who fail to meet hospital targets

explanation: You've got this! Quality improvement is simply about checking if our daily workflow changes are actually making patient care safer and better.

question: Which action by a nurse best demonstrates ongoing support for a grieving family after their loved one has passed away?

options.A: Encouraging them to forget the loss and return to work quickly
options.B: Billing the family promptly for grief counseling services
options.C: Sending a sympathy card or making a follow-up phone call weeks later
options.D: Avoiding contact to give them complete isolation

explanation: Small acts of ongoing outreach, such as a card or call, show the family they are remembered and supported through their grief journey. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h8)

question: How do common antacids neutralize stomach acid without needing cell receptors?

options.A: Through direct chemical reactions
options.B: By blocking hormone release
options.C: By stimulating enzyme production
options.D: By altering cellular DNA synthesis

explanation: Not all drugs need receptors! Antacids simply mix with stomach acid in a direct chemical reaction to calm the burning, just like chemistry in the lab.

question: Why is psychological safety so important for keeping quality high on a hospital ward?

options.A: It eliminates the need for nurses to document routine vital signs on shifts
options.B: It prevents patients from filing lawsuits against individual healthcare workers
options.C: It encourages staff to report errors and suggest changes without fear of punishment
options.D: It guarantees that the hospital will receive increased government funding every year

explanation: When nurses feel safe to speak up without getting into trouble, safety issues get fixed before anyone gets hurt.

question: What happens to a patient's pupils during the final, critical stage of severe asphyxia?

options.A: They remain normal and responsive
options.B: They blink rapidly back and forth
options.C: They dilate and stop reacting to light
options.D: They become very small and pinpoint

explanation: When the brain is starved of oxygen for too long, the brainstem gives up its pupillary reflexes, causing the pupils to dilate and stay fixed. Excellent assessment detail!

question: What does Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) allow nurses to do?

options.A: Print physical medication prescriptions automatically at home
options.B: Perform major surgical procedures over a live video stream
options.C: Replace all in-person nursing staff with computer software
options.D: Receive daily health readings sent from a patient's home device

explanation: RPM tools transmit vital signs and health metrics directly from the patient's home to healthcare providers for ongoing tracking. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h4)

question: Virginia Henderson is famous for giving us a clear checklist of fundamental human needs. How many are there on her list?
explanation: It's 14! Henderson outlined fourteen basic human needs that help us figure out exactly what kind of care our patients require.

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge faced by national disaster agencies?

options.A: Poor road networks and heavy traffic congestion during crises
options.B: Excessive funding and overabundance of modern rescue equipment
options.C: Infrastructural violations like buildings blocking natural waterways
options.D: Inadequate financial support and poor resource allocation

explanation: Sadly, disaster agencies usually struggle with a shortage of funds and equipment, rather than having too much! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is the main role of Langerhans cells in the epidermis?

options.A: Sensing touch and pressure changes in the environment
options.B: Fighting off invading pathogens and alerting the immune system
options.C: Producing waterproof oils to keep the skin surface soft
options.D: Storing excess fat for padding and insulation

explanation: Langerhans cells act as immune sentinels in the skin to catch invaders and trigger a defense response. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T5#GNS211_U2_T5_h2)

question: What does evidence-based nursing practice combine with research evidence?

options.A: Traditional hospital routines from the past
options.B: Financial costs of medical equipment
options.C: Personal opinions of the hospital director
options.D: Clinical expertise and patient values

explanation: True evidence-based practice brings together research findings, the nurse's clinical judgment, and the preferences of the patient. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h2)

question: What should a nurse do first when planning health education for a patient from a different cultural background?

options.A: Insist that the patient follow hospital routines strictly at home
options.B: Hand out standard English brochures without discussing them
options.C: Assume the patient already knows basic community health rules
options.D: Assess the patient's language, literacy level, and cultural beliefs

explanation: Education only works if the nurse understands how the patient communicates and what they believe about health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T2#GNS225_U2_T2_h5)

question: A nurse in a busy rural clinic runs out of sterile gloves during an emergency wound dressing. What is the safest clinical action?

options.A: Obtain fresh supplies or use available clean alternatives according to protocol, avoiding unsafe shortcuts
options.B: Cancel the procedure and send the patient home without care
options.C: Perform the procedure barehanded to save time
options.D: Reuse a discarded pair of gloves after washing them with cold water

explanation: Shortages should never excuse compromising basic safety; nurses must secure proper supplies or follow approved institutional alternatives. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h2)

question: Which drug do you keep on hand to reverse breathing difficulties in a newborn whose mother received strong pain meds during labor?

options.A: Adrenaline
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Atropine

explanation: Brilliant! Naloxone is an opioid blocker that quickly reverses respiratory depression caused by narcotic pain relief given during labor.

question: Why does Graves' disease cause hyperthyroidism?

options.A: The pituitary gland stops releasing any regulatory hormones
options.B: Dietary iodine levels become excessively high in the bloodstream
options.C: Thyroid tissue undergoes widespread autoimmune destruction
options.D: Antibodies mimic TSH and continuously stimulate the thyroid gland

explanation: In Graves' disease, rogue antibodies trick the thyroid by acting just like TSH (thyroid-stimulating hormone), forcing the gland to pump out way too much thyroid hormone.

question: Why does breastfeeding usually demand more energy and nutrition from a mother than pregnancy did?

options.A: Continuous milk synthesis requires daily energy and nutrient output
options.B: Mothers lose vital organs temporarily during the birth process
options.C: The infant grows much faster outside the womb than inside
options.D: Digestive efficiency drops significantly after childbirth occurs

explanation: Producing milk every single day is hard work for the body. It takes a steady, high daily supply of calories and nutrients to keep up with the growing baby!

question: In mental health care, what does a 'pluralistic healthcare system' mean?

options.A: Modern doctors refuse to speak with families of patients
options.B: There is only one universal hospital in the entire country
options.C: Traditional healers are legally banned from practicing medicine
options.D: Patients utilize both traditional healing and modern psychiatry

explanation: You're learning fast! A pluralistic system simply means people draw from multiple healthcare traditions, often moving between orthodox and traditional care.

question: A patient's CD4 count drops to what level to officially mark the transition from HIV to AIDS?

options.A: Below 1000 cells per microliter
options.B: Below 500 cells per microliter
options.C: Below 200 cells per microliter
options.D: Below 50 cells per microliter

explanation: Keep this number handy for the wards: when the CD4 count falls below 200 cells per microliter, the condition is classified as AIDS.

question: An older patient struggles to button their shirts because of stiff fingers from arthritis. What is the best nursing action to help them stay independent?

options.A: Insist that a family member dress the patient daily
options.B: Recommend adaptive clothing fasteners like Velcro
options.C: Tell the patient to stop wearing shirts altogether
options.D: Transfer the patient to a long-term care facility

explanation: Fantastic nursing thinking! Adaptive tools like Velcro help patients do things for themselves, boosting their confidence and maintaining their dignity.

question: Why must a researcher conduct a literature review early in the process?

options.A: To decide which nurses will be punished for mistakes
options.B: To see what is already known and avoid repeating past work
options.C: To find patients willing to participate in the study
options.D: To determine the exact financial cost of the hospital

explanation: Reading prior studies prevents wasting time on questions that have already been answered thoroughly. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the heart of reproductive rights?

options.A: The mandatory requirement for every adult to have children
options.B: Free cosmetic surgeries for all citizens reaching adulthood
options.C: Bodily autonomy and freedom from coercion in health decisions
options.D: Government control over family size and birth intervals

explanation: You nailed it! Reproductive rights mean every person has the right to make their own free choices about their body and family planning.
